source.title: Mechanistic interpretability of large language models with applications to the financial services industry
source.authors: Ashkan Golgoon; Khashayar Filom; Arjun Ravi Kannan

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses the IOI paper's direct logit attribution and activation-patching approach as a tool for a different task, fair-lending classification. It reports no new IOI results.
record.gate_note: The paper recounts the 26-head IOI circuit and its seven categories from cited work [39], but does not test that circuit. Its own GPT-2 Small experiments concern fair-lending prompts, not IOI. The paper says path patching is future work. Own fair-lending results are recorded as findings that fit none of the IOI claim versions.
record.test_reason: The paper borrows the IOI paper's logit-difference metric, direct logit attribution and activation patching, and applies them to GPT-2 Small on fair-lending prompts. It runs no IOI experiments: no circuit evaluation, no name-mover ablation, no other models, no method comparison on IOI and no IOI prompt variants. Its remarks contrasting the task with IOI, such as MLPs mattering and contributions building across layers, compare against cited results, not new IOI measurements.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors find that fair-lending task completion in GPT-2 Small involves many heads and MLP layers. Patching highlights heads 10.2, 10.7, 11.3 (positive) and 9.6, 10.6 (negative), plus head 10.2's value vector and the query/key vectors of layer-0 heads 0.5, 0.1 and 0.10. Path patching and an end-to-end circuit are left for future work.
record.recipe_differences: The paper adapts direct logit attribution and activation patching from the IOI circuit-analysis approach to a fair-lending task, with different prompts and output metrics. It does not perform path patching or test the IOI circuit.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports differing contributions across layers, heads, token positions and attention components for the fair-lending task; it does not compare alternative evaluation methods or prompt distributions for IOI.

fits_no_version.finding: On fair-lending prompts, GPT-2 Small averages logit difference 0.81 and P(Yes)/P(No) of 2.26. Attribution and patching implicate MLP layers and several heads, some of which are IOI circuit heads (0.1, 0.10, 9.6, 9.9, 10.7, 10.10, 11.10), without any role analysis.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: GPT-2 Small's fair-lending yes/no classification draws on MLP layers and many attention heads, including some heads that belong to the IOI circuit.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on AI in Finance
record.problems: The paper reports fair-lending results on a small prompt set, including patching results averaged over 4 prompts. It reports no uncertainty estimates. Many plotted results are qualitative in the text, and it does not complete an end-to-end circuit analysis or perform path patching.
record.rows_left_out: Numeric values for individual layers, heads, token positions and component-patching scores in Figures 9–18 are not stated in the text and were not extracted from the figures. The paper's prose descriptions of the principal findings are recorded in R3–R14.

untested.parts: No IOI test of the 26-head circuit, its classes, or faithfulness, completeness and minimality.
No ablation of name-mover heads; no self-repair test.
No other models, sizes or checkpoints. Fair-lending heads overlap with IOI heads, but no role-level reuse test.
No comparison of circuit-finding methods, ablations or metrics on IOI.
No IOI name-order, template or more-names tests.

record.verdict_notes: The IOI circuit is only recounted from the original source [39]. Several heads the paper finds important for fair lending coincide with IOI circuit heads. This is potentially relevant to V3 component reuse, but the authors neither note nor test it, so no verdict is given. Results come from 4 patching prompts and no uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: No IOI test of the circuit, head classes or faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria.
No ablation of IOI name-mover heads or test of self-repair.
No cross-model, cross-size, checkpoint or task-reuse test of the IOI circuit.
No comparison of circuit-finding methods, ablation types or evaluation metrics on IOI.
No test of IOI evaluation sensitivity to ablation, metric or prompt distribution.
No IOI test across name orders, templates or numbers of names.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small
rows.operation_detail: Patched clean-run residual-stream activations into corrupted runs at the start of each layer.

conditions.value: 4 fair-lending prompts; results averaged over all 4

rows.measure: Recovery of the clean response, assessed by residual-stream patching score
rows.baseline: Corrupted-input performance corresponds to a score closer to 0; clean-input performance corresponds to a score closer to 1.
rows.value: The computation is described as localized to positions 22, 29, 42, 44, 54 and END; information at position 22 begins moving to END around layers 5 and 6.
rows.note: The stated position-level findings concern fair-lending prompts, not IOI.

rows.value: Layers 8 and 10 contribute positively; layer 9 contributes negatively. MLP-05 and MLP-11 are described as important.
rows.note: Qualitative patching results for a different task.
